In the 49th minute, Andre Clovis thought he had extended the lead further, but a VAR review ruled the goal out for offside. This let-off sparked a resurgence from Maritimo , who began to dominate possession and territory. Their persistence finally paid off in the 70th minute when Paulo Henrique found the net with a clinical left-footed strike to make it 1-2. The match grew increasingly physical as both sides battled for control, with the referee busy issuing yellow cards to maintain order. Maritimo manager made several tactical changes, including bringing on Bryan Limbombe , to maintain the pressure as the clock ticked down toward the final ten minutes. Late Penalty Drama and Red Card The defining moment of the comeback arrived in the 84th minute. Andre Ceitil was penalized for tripping Adrian Butzke inside the box, handing Maritimo a golden opportunity from the penalty spot. Butzke stepped up himself in the 88th minute, coolly sending Ewerton the wrong way to equalize and send the home fans into raptures. There was still time for more drama in stoppage time. In the 90th+4 minute, Bruno Pinheiro was shown a straight red card for dissent after verbally abusing the referee. Despite the numerical advantage for the final moments, Maritimo couldn't find a winner, and a pulsating match ended in a hard-fought draw.
